chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, similar to it.
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: I asked him about the thing which is placed on the road, so the animal passes by, so it panics and fells its rider. So he said: Everything which harms the Muslims on the road, so its owner is responsible for what (harm) it causes.

key_terms.تَعْقِرُهُ: It injures/disables him (specifically regarding the leg or joint)

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for injuries caused by objects placed on public roads in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, establishes the principle of *daman* (liability) for any obstacle placed on public thoroughfares that causes harm, extending beyond wells to include any object that startles animals or injures passersby. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often linked to the concept of *darar* (harm) and the owner's responsibility to ensure public safety, reflecting the broader legal maxim that 'harm shall not be inflicted or reciprocated.' The ruling underscores the social obligation of Muslims to maintain clear paths, with the owner bearing full financial compensation for resulting injuries.
